planting.note: Set crowns 1-2 inches below soil level in humus-rich, consistently moist ground; shelter from drying wind to protect the large palmate leaves.

directions: Divide established clumps in early spring and replant promptly so roots do not dry out. Leaves emerge bronze and darken toward deep red-purple with bronze highlights as the season progresses. Bright pink flower plumes rise on reddish stems in early to midsummer above the horse-chestnut-shaped foliage. Keep soil reliably moist and mulch to conserve moisture in hot weather.

planting.note: Plant divisions in reliably moist, humus-rich soil; a compact selection well suited to smaller shade borders.

directions: This compact leopard plant forms clumps of leathery, deep purple-bronze leaves with mahogany undersides, noticeably smaller in stature than most Ligularia dentata selections. Vivid orange-yellow daisy flowers rise on sturdy stems in late summer. Keep soil consistently moist, since leaves wilt visibly in dry spells and midday sun. Mulch and partial afternoon shade help retain foliage quality through summer heat.

planting.note: A patented variegated sport of 'Desdemona'; propagate only by authorized division due to plant breeders' rights protection.

directions: Introduced by Terra Nova Nurseries as a variegated sport of the familiar 'Desdemona', this selection carries irregular cream-and-gold leaves splashed with lime and magenta tones, with purple undersides. Orange-yellow daisy flowerheads appear above the foliage in late summer. Grow in consistently moist, rich soil with protection from midday sun to prevent leaf scorch and to keep the variegation from fading.

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring or fall; colonizes gradually in humus-rich woodland soil.

directions: A Walters Gardens introduction prized for its bright red, upright, gently arching stems that stay red from base to tip. Dark green leaves with silvery undersides line the stalks, and paired white bell flowers dangle from the leaf axils in late spring, followed by blue berries in autumn. Grow in part to full shade with steady moisture; established colonies spread gradually by rhizome.

planting.note: A dwarf, stoloniferous selection best used as a small-scale woodland groundcover; keep evenly moist.

directions: This dwarf fairy bells selection spreads gradually as a low woodland groundcover, with rounded lance-shaped leaves marked by a bold central band of creamy white variegation that fades from yellow emergence. Small pendulous creamy white and green bell flowers dangle beneath the foliage in spring. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in mostly shaded sites, dividing clumps to spread the groundcover where wanted.

planting.note: Slower-spreading Japanese selection than the common white-edged form; divide in spring.

directions: A Japanese selection of fairy bells that spreads more slowly than the common white-edged form. Stalks emerge in mid-spring clothed in green leaves heavily streaked with yellow, with the streaking shifting toward white over summer and often merging into a near-solid pale leaf center. Small white bell flowers hang beneath the foliage in spring. Grow in light to full shade with even moisture for best leaf coloring.
